To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

elevated PKM2 and mitochondrial biogenesis enzymes in the kidney and circulation are associated with preservation of renal structure and function in type 1 and 3b chronic diabetic kidney disease (CKDu).
the renal profile of elevated glucose metabolism enzymes and reduced toxic metabolites is reflected by the circulation and can be used as a biomarker for endogenous renal protection.
the elevation of enzymes involved in metabolism of intracellular glucose and its metabolite is connected to preservation of kidney function in both T1 and T2 diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for the prevention of diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
the identification of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of diabetic nephropathies and other complications of diabetes.
the development of novel therapies for diabetic nephropathy based on the identification of endogenous renal protective mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the glycolytic enzymes, in particular, pyruvates kinase M2 (and M1), and enolase, are elevated in renal glomerular tissue in type 1 and 3b chronic diabetic nephropathy and in plasma of Medalist Study subjects with type 1 (and type 2) diabetes and no chronic kidney disease.
the Medalists’ renal protection is due to increased glycolytic and reduced mitochondrial metabolism.

the elevation of enzymes involved in metabolism of intracellular glucose and its metabolite is associated with preserving kidney function in people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes, and that the renal profile of elevated glucose metabolism and reduced toxic glucose metabolism is reflected in the plasma of people with diabetes, supporting their use in biomarker development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
elevated glycolytic flux in the renal glomeruli and improved mitochondrial biogenisis is a protective factor against diabetic nephropathy in both type 2 diabetes as well as the Medalists cohort.
the glycolytic enzymes, including PKM2, are upregulated in the kidney of Medalists and in their circulation and may be a biomarker of renal protection.

the Medalist cohort is a unique resource to study diabetic complications and that the proteomic and metabolomic screens have identified novel circulating biomarkers for diabetic nephropathy and renal preservation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the renal profile of elevated enzymes involved in the glycolysis pathway is reflected in the blood of Medalists with type 2 and type 1 diabetes, suggesting that they may be useful biomarkers for endogenously generated renal protective factors.

there are endogenous factors within the body that can protect the kidney in diabetes, and that we can use this information to develop new therapies to prevent or slow the progression of diabetic kidney disease.
the renal protection seen in Medalists is not limited to individuals with long-duration type 1 diabetes, but also extends to those with type 2 disease.
